author: GamingBolt
description:
Onimusha: Way of the Sword is the newest Onimusha game, arriving after the series took a 20-year gap. It was one of my favourite action series back in the day and I still remember playing it on my PS2 for hours on end. So in anticipation of Way of the Sword, we will look at the entire Onimusha series story in chronological order. 

Please note that this video includes the first three Onimusha games we previously covered, and as a bonus, we've also included the full recap of Dawn of Dreams, something we haven’t covered before. So, let’s start right away.
title: Onimusha: The Complete Story - The Definitive Recap Before Onimusha: Way of the Sword

author: GamingBolt
description:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is bringing an innovative new approach to its RPG systems, and there are a few concerns about how those additions might affect the open-world experience it’s trying to offer. We’re here to put your fears to rest and explain how this one isn’t just a great title, but an eye-opener for other RPGs in modern gaming.

We’ve got our reasons for saying so, with the time mechanic being a lynchpin in our arguments. Join us as we dive into the nitty gritties of what makes Rebel Wolves’ debut title tick as you uncover more of Vale Sangora, and get more involved in Coen’s troubles.
title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Has Solved One of Open World RPGs' BIGGEST Problems

author: GamingBolt
description:
The much-awaited expansion to Crimson Desert has finally been revealed, and Pywel’s about to become a hotbed of Greymane activity next month. Of course, the seas are now open to us while things on land have created the need for a more serious base for the Greymanes. Fortunately, Kliff, Damiane, Oongka, and the rest of the group are more than up to the task. But can the same be said for the expansion’s effort to bring new content to a game that’s so chock full of it?

We’d say yes, as it isn’t just new content, but new ways to enjoy it all that make this one a potential gold mine for Crimson Desert's players. We’ve gone in depth about why, so tune in and allow us to convince you about what you already suspect: Charting the Unknown is a potentially great expansion thanks to what its trying to achieve.
title: Crimson Desert’s Charting the Unknown Is Doing Something Most Open-World DLC Never Does
